hunks.baseline: There was nothing particularly positive about suspecting someone.
hunks.sol: Suspecting someone was hardly a good thing.

hunks.baseline: But in a time of war like this, suspicion was just another word for caution.
hunks.sol: But in a time of war, suspicion was another word for caution.

hunks.baseline: The more you looked, and the deeper you dug, the clearer the truth became—and the closer you came to victory.
hunks.sol: The longer and more closely you looked, the clearer the truth became—and the closer you came to victory.

hunks.baseline: That was the biggest reason Ma Junggeol and the other six masters of Baekma Bang had joined our group.
hunks.sol: That was the main reason Ma Junggeol and the Seven Masters of Baekma Bang had joined our party.

hunks.baseline: *Though I was the one who stepped forward and volunteered.*
hunks.sol: *Though I was the one who volunteered to take them.*

hunks.baseline: They were originally supposed to be placed under Sima Gong’s watch. But when I explained that he had his hands full commanding a sizable force, we reached a decision in no time.
hunks.sol: They were originally supposed to be placed under Sima Gong’s watch. But when I pointed out that he already had a sizable force to command, the decision came quickly.

hunks.baseline: We were in such a hurry that no one raised any further objections. Still, I saw it clearly.
hunks.sol: Time was so short that no one raised any further objections. Still, I saw it clearly.

hunks.baseline: The moment the decision about the Seven Masters of Baekma Bang was made, Sima Gong’s eyes sank deeper than before.
hunks.sol: The moment the decision was made, Sima Gong’s gaze darkened.

hunks.baseline: The horses’ hooves thundered as they galloped, and the fierce wind coiled around us and rushed past.
hunks.sol: Hooves thundered beneath us. A fierce wind wrapped around my body and rushed past.

hunks.baseline: And…
hunks.sol: And through it all…

hunks.baseline: A faint ripple passed stealthily through it all.
hunks.sol: A faint ripple reached me, almost hidden by the noise.

hunks.baseline: I could feel it instinctively.
This was a flow of energy only someone who had reached a profound realm could sense.
hunks.sol: I knew it instinctively. It was a flow of qi only someone who had reached a profound realm could sense.

hunks.baseline: And within that faint ripple, carried to me beneath the clamor of countless sounds, was a voice I’d never heard before.
hunks.sol: Buried beneath the pounding hooves and rushing wind, that faint ripple carried a voice I had never heard before.

hunks.baseline: This wasn’t some calculated conclusion I’d reached through reason. It was an instinct I’d forgotten I had.
hunks.sol: I hadn’t reasoned it out. This was an instinct I’d forgotten for a moment.

hunks.baseline: Like a child who had only just learned to stand on two feet, I sent my qi toward the ripple emanating from Ma Junggeol.
hunks.sol: Like a child just discovering he could stand on two feet, I sent my qi toward the ripple emanating from Ma Junggeol.

hunks.baseline: It touched the ripple, mingled with it, and soon became one.
hunks.sol: It touched, mingled with, and became one with the ripple.

hunks.baseline: So naturally that even Ma Junggeol, the ripple’s source, didn’t notice.
hunks.sol: So naturally that even Ma Junggeol, its source, didn’t notice.

hunks.baseline: Nor did his six sworn brothers, who were exchanging the same kind of ripples with one another not far away.
hunks.sol: The same went for the ripples his six sworn brothers were exchanging nearby.

hunks.baseline: “…How long do we have to be dragged along like this?”
hunks.sol: “…long do we have to be dragged along like this?”

hunks.baseline: That was the moment the faint ripple—no, the Sound Transmission—rang clearly in my ears at last.
hunks.sol: The faint ripple—no, the Sound Transmission—rang clearly in my ears at last.

hunks.baseline:
> **System**  
> Hidden achievement **A Bug in My Ear** achieved!  
> You can now detect and eavesdrop on nearby **Sound Transmissions**!  
> This is another ability granted to those who reach a great realm. But don’t get too excited. The **Sound Transmissions** you can eavesdrop on are limited by the levels of both the target and the user!
hunks.sol:

>
> Hidden achievement **A Bug in My Ear** achieved!

hunks.baseline: I blinked in a daze for a moment, then focused on the Sound Transmissions reaching my ears.
hunks.sol: I blinked in a daze, then focused on the Sound Transmissions reaching my ears.

hunks.baseline: Let’s hear what sort of conspiracy they’re cooking up.
hunks.sol: Let’s hear what they’re plotting.

hunks.baseline: At his younger brothers’ grumbling Sound Transmissions, Ma Junggeol answered in a stern voice.
hunks.sol: Ma Junggeol answered his younger brothers’ grumbling Sound Transmissions sternly.

hunks.baseline: “Now, now. Why are you all complaining so much? We expected this from the start.”
hunks.sol: “Now, now. Why are you all complaining? We expected this from the start.”

hunks.baseline: The second brother, who fled faster than anyone in an emergency but worshipped the Chief like the heavens the rest of the time, nodded.
hunks.sol: The second brother, who would flee faster than anyone in an emergency but otherwise revered his eldest brother like the heavens, nodded.

hunks.baseline: “Enough! The Chief is a hundred, a thousand times right, so all of you shut up. If he hadn’t foreseen a situation like this from the beginning, would he have dragged us into such a deathtrap?”
hunks.sol: “Enough! The Chief is a hundred, a thousand times right, so all of you shut up. If he hadn’t foreseen this from the beginning, would he have dragged us into such a deathtrap?”

hunks.baseline: Just then, Ma Junggeol smiled with satisfaction at the sight of the little man gently putting the others in their place.
hunks.sol: Ma Junggeol smiled with satisfaction as the little man gently put the others in their place.

hunks.baseline: At the third brother’s abrupt remark—he always had to stick his foot in everything—the second brother blinked.
hunks.sol: The third brother, who always had to stick his foot in, broke in. The second blinked.

hunks.baseline: “Right before we left. He wandered off on his own, supposedly to check a perfectly good saddle, and muttered something in a tiny voice. I listened, and…”
hunks.sol: “Right before we left. He went off by himself, supposedly to check a perfectly good saddle, and started muttering under his breath. I listened, and…”

hunks.baseline: “You listened, and?”
hunks.sol: “And?”

hunks.baseline: Remembering what he’d said half a shichen earlier, Ma Junggeol hurriedly tried to cut him off. But the third brother’s Sound Transmission was already riding the wind.
hunks.sol: Ma Junggeol remembered what had happened half a shichen earlier and hurried to cut him off. But the third brother’s Sound Transmission was already riding the wind.

hunks.baseline: “We’re fucked. What do we do now?”
hunks.sol: “He said, ‘We’re fucked. What do we do now?’”

hunks.baseline: A wind colder than the bitter north wind swept through the group.
hunks.sol: A wind colder than the bitter northern winter swept through the group.

hunks.baseline: In the heavy silence that fell, six pairs of eyes bored mercilessly into the back of Ma Junggeol’s head. His eyes sank darkly.
hunks.sol: In the heavy silence, six pairs of eyes bored mercilessly into the back of Ma Junggeol’s head. His gaze darkened.

hunks.baseline: “What do you mean, ‘there’s no way’? I heard it with my own ears.”
hunks.sol: “What do you mean, ‘there’s no way’? I heard him with my own ears.”

hunks.baseline: How was he supposed to answer that?
hunks.sol: How was he supposed to answer? He’d never dreamed anyone would hear the words he’d let slip—least of all the third brother.

hunks.baseline: He’d never dreamed the third brother would hear him mutter to himself—especially when he’d let it slip without thinking.
Unable to stay silent forever, he hesitantly sent his reply.
hunks.sol: Unable to stay silent forever, he sent a hesitant reply.

hunks.baseline: At once, his six perceptive brothers let out a collective groan.
hunks.sol: His six quick-witted brothers groaned at once.

hunks.baseline: “Sometimes it’s like that. You miss them all the more when they passed away so long ago.”
hunks.sol: “Sometimes it’s like that. When someone passed away long ago, you miss them all the more.”

hunks.baseline: “Chief, what are we actually going to do now? At this rate, they’ll drag us all the way to the front and use us to catch swords, won’t they?”
hunks.sol: “Chief, what are we actually going to do? At this rate, they’ll drag us all the way to the front and use us to catch swords, won’t they?”

hunks.baseline: Unlike the others, who were caught up in the chaos, the third brother was at least facing reality. Ma Junggeol gave the faintest shake of his head.
hunks.sol: Unlike the others, who had descended into confusion, the third brother was at least facing reality. Ma Junggeol gave the faintest shake of his head.

hunks.baseline: “Don’t worry. Things are going a little—just a little—worse than I expected, but they won’t use us to catch swords like you said.”
hunks.sol: “Don’t worry. Things are going a little—just a little—worse than I expected, but they won’t use us to catch swords.”

hunks.baseline: “If it’s not swords, they’ll use us to catch arrows. Thanks, Chief. You’ve ruined all our lives.”
hunks.sol: “If it’s not swords, it’ll be arrows. Thanks, Chief. You’ve ruined all our lives.”

hunks.baseline: “Then what are you basing that confidence on, Chief? Let’s be blunt. If they tell us to jump, we have to ask how high, don’t we?”
hunks.sol: “What makes you so sure? Let’s be blunt. If they give us an order, we’re in no position to refuse.”

hunks.baseline: “Take a look around. There are already several Supreme Peak masters here—people you’d be lucky to see once in your life. If those monsters start prodding us in the back and giving us the look, what choice do guys like us have except to sprint out and fight like hell?”
hunks.sol: “Look around. There are already several Supreme Peak masters here—people you’d be lucky to see once in your life. If those monsters start prodding us in the back and giving us the look, what choice do guys like us have except to run out and fight like hell?”

hunks.baseline: The third brother’s Sound Transmission sounded like an outpouring of pent-up anger. His sworn brothers chimed in one after another.
hunks.sol: The third brother’s Sound Transmission poured out with pent-up anger. His sworn brothers joined in.

hunks.baseline: “There are those Zhongnan Sect Daoist punks treating us like outright bandits, the Black Night King himself, the Fire King, and that young Disciple of his who looks half-mad.”
hunks.sol: “There are those Zhongnan Sect Daoists treating us like common bandits, the Black Night King himself, the Fire King, and that young disciple of his who seems half-mad.”

hunks.baseline: “Especially that Jin Taekyung standing right in front of the Chief. He’s not right in the head. Have you forgotten how we nearly crossed the Sanzu River[^1] before we’d even made it through the gate?”
hunks.sol: “Especially that Jin Taekyung right in front of the Chief. He’s not right in the head. Have you forgotten how we nearly crossed the Sanzu River[^1] before we’d even made it through the gate?”

hunks.baseline: “Damn it, is this why we quit being mounted bandits? I’ll admit our past wasn’t exactly something to brag about, but we quit before we’d even gotten to rob anyone! We spent all day, every day sharpening our swords and never even got to draw them.”
hunks.sol: “Damn it, is this why we quit being mounted bandits? I’ll admit our past wasn’t exactly something to brag about, but we quit before we’d robbed anyone! We spent all day, every day sharpening our swords and never even got to draw them.”

hunks.baseline: “Enough! Now that I think about it, this is downright unfair. Have we robbed anyone? Killed any innocent civilians? We were just about to get our act together and pull off one decent score when we met the Lord and turned over a new leaf. We’re trying to live a little more honestly, and this is just too much.”
hunks.sol: “Enough! Now that I think about it, this is downright unfair. Have we robbed anyone? Killed any innocent civilians? We’d only just made up our minds to pull off one good score when we met Great Sir and turned over a new leaf. We’re trying to live decent lives, and this is what we get?”

hunks.baseline: “Second Brother’s right. Sure, we look like this, but if we’d gone around doing only the most vicious things like everyone else, do you think the Lord would’ve left us alone? Isn’t that right?”
hunks.sol: “Second Brother’s right. Sure, we look like this, but if we’d gone around committing every vicious crime we could, like the other bastards, do you think Great Sir would’ve left us alone? Well?”

hunks.baseline: Listening to their Sound Transmissions, brimming with sorrow, Ma Junggeol felt a pang in his own heart.
hunks.sol: Their Sound Transmissions were full of wounded indignation. Listening to them, Ma Junggeol felt a pang in his own heart.

hunks.baseline: Of course, he couldn’t deny that he used to be a mounted bandit. But he could swear to heaven that they’d never done anything deserving punishment.
hunks.sol: He couldn’t deny that they used to be mounted bandits. But he could swear to heaven that they’d never done anything deserving punishment.

hunks.baseline: *If we’d actually done those things, at least this treatment wouldn’t feel so unfair.*
hunks.sol: *If we had, at least this treatment wouldn’t feel so unfair.*

hunks.baseline: Even when they steeled themselves and rode out to attack, they couldn’t bring themselves to do a thing.
hunks.sol: Even when they steeled themselves and rode out to attack, they couldn’t bring themselves to do it.

hunks.baseline: What could they take from people who’d already been stripped of everything by other mounted-bandit groups? Countless times, they’d even given away their own food to families holding newborns too hungry to cry.
hunks.sol: What could they take from people other mounted bandits had already stripped bare? Countless times, they’d given food instead to families holding newborns too hungry to cry.

hunks.baseline: Although they looked like fiends, Ma Junggeol and his six sworn brothers were timid by nature.
hunks.sol: They might have looked like fiends, but Ma Junggeol and his six sworn brothers were timid by nature.

hunks.baseline: Robbing or killing civilians had been impossible for them from the start. And even when they occasionally came across a gutsy merchant caravan traveling to Ningxia Province, they just collected a toll and let it pass.
hunks.sol: Robbing or killing civilians had been beyond them from the start. Even when they occasionally encountered a merchant caravan bold enough to travel through Ningxia Province, they only collected a toll and let it pass.

hunks.baseline: It was only natural for an Escort Bureau or merchant caravan to bring at least several dozen armed men. In that tense standoff, Ma Junggeol just had to put on his vicious face and say:
hunks.sol: Any Escort Bureau or merchant caravan would naturally bring at least several dozen armed men. In the tense standoff that followed, Ma Junggeol only had to show them his fearsome face and ask:

hunks.baseline: A fiendish-looking face paired with a stern voice made for an excellent negotiating tactic.
hunks.sol: A face to rival any fiend’s, paired with a stern voice, made an excellent way to talk things over.

hunks.baseline: Back then, Ma Junggeol and his six sworn brothers knew little about martial arts. That was how Ma Junggeol and his six sworn brothers, whose martial arts were still rudimentary back then, had survived as a mounted-bandit group.
hunks.sol: That was how Ma Junggeol and his six sworn brothers had survived as mounted bandits back when their martial arts were still rudimentary.

hunks.baseline: Until the man they called “the Lord” appeared.
hunks.sol: Until the man they called Great Sir appeared.

hunks.baseline: And even now, Ma Junggeol firmly believed in the Lord who had led them onto the right path.
hunks.sol: Even now, Ma Junggeol firmly believed in the man who had led them onto the right path.

hunks.baseline: At Ma Junggeol’s forceful Sound Transmission, the grievances streaming from behind him cut off at once.
hunks.sol: At his forceful Sound Transmission, the complaints streaming from behind him stopped at once.

hunks.sol: Ma Junggeol seized the brief opening.

hunks.baseline: “There’s nothing to worry about. Even if you don’t trust me, surely you trust that the Lord would have anticipated a situation like this?”
hunks.sol: “There’s nothing to worry about. Set me aside—surely Great Sir anticipated a situation like this?”

hunks.baseline: “If it’s the Lord, that’s different. The Chief, maybe not, but the Lord, yes.”
hunks.sol: “The Chief might not have, but Great Sir is different.”

hunks.baseline: “Right. We can’t trust the Chief, but we can trust the Lord.”
hunks.sol: “Right. We can’t trust the Chief, but we can trust Great Sir.”

hunks.baseline: “Now that you mention it, that makes sense.”
hunks.sol: “Now that you mention it…”

hunks.baseline: The answers only made him feel stranger the longer he thought about them, but Ma Junggeol continued his Sound Transmission with a vague sense of unease.
hunks.sol: The more Ma Junggeol thought about their answers, the stranger they felt. He continued his Sound Transmission anyway.

hunks.baseline: “I sent a few men back on the pretext of relaying news to Ningxia, so the Lord will surely hear about this. Until then, don’t do anything rash. Understood?”
hunks.sol: “I sent a few men back on the pretext of relaying news to Ningxia, so Great Sir will hear about this. Until then, don’t do anything rash. Understood?”

hunks.baseline: Just then, the third brother, the one with the bulbous nose, cut in.
hunks.sol: The third brother, the one with the bulbous nose, cut in.

hunks.baseline: “But that’s only if the Lord’s in his right mind.”
hunks.sol: “But that’s only if Great Sir’s in his right mind.”

hunks.baseline: “Well, isn’t it? You know as well as anyone how he can be a little… all over the place.”
hunks.sol: “Well, you know as well as anyone how he can be a little… all over the place.”

hunks.baseline: But even without Ma Junggeol’s uncertain answer, his sworn brothers knew it was something no one could be sure about.
hunks.sol: Even without his uncertain answer, his sworn brothers knew no one could be sure of that.

hunks.baseline: “But hasn’t the Lord been more or less all right lately? That’s why he’s been telling us this and that about the direction we should head.”
hunks.sol: “But hasn’t Great Sir been more or less all right lately? That’s why he’s been telling us where to go from here and all that.”

hunks.baseline: “The Lord was strange from the first time we met him. His hair was a complete mess, and his face was so black he looked like he hadn’t washed in days. He was a regular beggar. He still looks the same now, too.”
hunks.sol: “Great Sir was strange from the first time we met him. His hair was a tangled mess, and his face was so black with grime you’d think he hadn’t washed in days. He looked like a beggar. Still does.”

hunks.baseline: “This is bad. If the Lord’s off his rocker right now, sending the men to him will be useless, won’t it?”
hunks.sol: “This is bad. If Great Sir’s out of it right now, sending the men to him won’t do any good, will it?”

hunks.baseline: As his sworn brothers’ worry deepened, Ma Junggeol scrunched up his already ugly face and thought it over. At last, he spoke.
hunks.sol: As his sworn brothers’ worry deepened, Ma Junggeol scrunched up his already ugly face and thought hard. At last, he spoke.

hunks.baseline: “We have no choice. One of us should go in person. Maybe seeing some familiar faces he sees often will help him come to his senses sooner.”
hunks.sol: “We have no choice. One of us should go in person. Seeing a face he knows well might help him come to his senses sooner.”

hunks.baseline: “Hard to say. We’ll have to decide now.”
hunks.sol: “I don’t know. We’ll have to decide.”

hunks.baseline: “Once we decide, how are you going to send him? That’ll be difficult in our current situation.”
hunks.sol: “And once we do, how are you going to send him? That’ll be difficult right now.”

hunks.baseline: “As the Chief, I’ll figure that out, so don’t worry—wait a minute.”
hunks.sol: “As the Chief, I’ll take care of that, so don’t worry—wait a minute.”

hunks.baseline: “You’ve been getting awful casual with me for a while now. Did you lose half your tongue or something? Which insolent bastard is it? Huh?”
hunks.sol: “You’ve been awfully casual with me for a while now. Did you lose half your tongue or something? Which insolent bastard is it? Huh?”

hunks.baseline: That was the exact moment.
Someone’s actual voice, from someone he hadn’t expected, pierced Ma Junggeol’s ears.
hunks.sol: At that very moment, an actual voice he hadn’t expected reached his ears.

hunks.baseline: “It’s me.”
hunks.sol: “I said it’s me.”

hunks.baseline: No. Impossible. Surely not.
hunks.sol: *No. Impossible. Surely not.*

hunks.baseline: Muttering to himself, Ma Junggeol slowly raised his head. He’d been keeping it slightly lowered to hide his moving lips.
hunks.sol: Ma Junggeol slowly raised his head. He’d been keeping it slightly lowered to hide the movement of his lips.

hunks.baseline: And there, facing him, was that insolent bastard, smiling menacingly.
hunks.sol: There, facing him, was that insolent bastard, smiling menacingly.

hunks.baseline: Ma Junggeol shuddered as if possessed by a ghost. Jin Taekyung smiled warmly at him.
hunks.sol: Ma Junggeol trembled as if he’d seen a ghost. Jin Taekyung gave him a gentle smile.
